verses.1: After these things, King Ahşverosh grew up. He then carried the man of Magdala to the Agag Temple and placed his throne above all the kings who were there.
verses.2: And all the servants of the king, who were in the king’s courtyard, bowed and prostrated themselves before Haman. For so commanded the king. But Mordecai did not bow or prostrate himself before Haman.
verses.3: And the servants of the king said to Mordecai, “Why do you disobey the commands of the king?”
verses.4: And as they said to him day after day, he still did not listen to them. So they told Hamán that Mordecai’s words had been fulfilled, because he had indeed told them what would happen.
verses.5: And the man saw that there was no one to help him or to worship him. So, the man became angry.
verses.6: And he decided to send his hand against Mordecai alone, because they had told him about the people of Mordecai. He wanted to destroy all the Jews who lived in all of Ahşverosh’s kingdoms.
verses.7: In the first month, which is Nisan, in the twenty-second year of King Ahashverosh’s reign, the plow fell down before the sun. From day to day, month after month, until the twenty-second year of his reign… It was Adar.
verses.8: And Haman said to King Ahashusha, “There is a people who have been scattered and separated from the other nations in all your kingdoms. Their religion is different from that of all other nations. They do not follow the laws and traditions of the king. The king has no way to deal with them.”
verses.9: If there is good written about the king, it will be recorded for his benefit. And twelve thousand pieces of silver will be paid by those who work in the palace, so that they can bring them to the king’s prisons.
verses.10: And the king took his crown off his head and gave it to Haman, the persecutor of the Jews.
verses.11: And the king said to Haman, “The money has been given to you, and the people should use it in a good way, according to your opinion.”
verses.12: And the officials of the king called together all those who were under his command, over twelve days. They wrote down everything that Ahşadrafnei the king had commanded them to do. They also wrote down the names of the people and tribes from various countries. All these names were recorded in the handwriting of the king Ahşverosh.
verses.13: And the scribes will be sent by the king to all the nations, in order to destroy and kill all the Jews, from boy to old man. This will happen on one day, in three dozen days. It’s the month Adar.
verses.14: The law of Pashkegen aims to provide a religion in every country, and for all nations to have access to it, so that it can be a standard for today’s times.
verses.15: The nobles went out in a hurry to hear the king’s words. The law was given in the royal palace. The king and his men sat down to drink. And the city of Shushan became quiet.
